title: South America capitals one of three · The North and the Caribbean Coast
edition: South America capitals · Three regional lessons · John · November 2026
intro: Welcome to the South America capitals, episode one of three. First, I clear the chosen names for a fresh regional lesson.
We begin in the north: the Andean capitals of Venezuela, Colombia and Ecuador, and the two Guianas on the Atlantic coast.

states.name: Caracas
lines: Caracas stands in a valley of the northern Andes, a dozen kilometres inland from the Caribbean, with the wall of El Ávila rising between the city and the sea.
Named for the Caracas people who lived in the valley, it was the birthplace of Simón Bolívar in 1783.
Remember Caracas as the city of Bolívar, tucked under the wall of Ávila between the mountains and the Caribbean.

states.name: Georgetown
lines: Georgetown stands on the Atlantic coast of Guyana, at the mouth of the Demerara river, a little north of the Essequibo.
Named for King George III, its wooden St George's Cathedral is one of the tallest wooden churches in the world, and much of the city lies below sea level behind a sea wall of the 19th century.
Remember Georgetown as the wooden cathedral capital, guarded by the sea wall that holds back the Atlantic.

states.name: Paramaribo
lines: Paramaribo lies on the Suriname river, about fifteen kilometres from the Atlantic, on the north coast of Suriname.
Its inner city of wooden Dutch colonial houses is a UNESCO site, and a mosque and a synagogue stand side by side on the same street.
Remember Paramaribo as the Dutch wooden town where a mosque and a synagogue share one street.

states.name: Bogotá
lines: Bogotá lies high in the eastern Andes, on a plateau about 2,640 metres above the sea, in the centre of Colombia.

It grew from Bacatá, the Muisca capital, meaning "enclosure outside the farmland"; the Spanish added Santa Fe, and the two names competed for centuries. Its Gold Museum holds some 55,000 pieces of pre-Hispanic goldwork.
Remember Bogotá as the high plateau capital where the Muisca Bacatá and the Spanish Santa Fe still share the name.

states.name: Quito
lines: Quito stands in the Andes of Ecuador at about 2,850 metres above the sea, a capital city on the equator.
Its old centre was among the first places added to UNESCO's World Heritage list, in 1978, and it lies below the Pichincha volcano, which last erupted in 1999.
Remember Quito as the capital of the equator, one of the first on UNESCO's list, sitting under a volcano that erupted in 1999.

recap: Caracas sits under the Ávila wall by the Caribbean, Bogotá and Quito climb high into the Andes, and Georgetown and Paramaribo are the two small colonial ports of the Guianas.
Remember the city of Bolívar, the wooden cathedral of Georgetown, the wooden Dutch houses of Paramaribo, the equator capital under a volcano, and the gold of Bacatá.
